description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related metrics (Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy) vary as a function of Initial Confidence. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.86 to 1.00 with tick labels at about 0.86, 0.88, 0.89, 0.90, 0.91, 0.92, 0.93, 0.94, 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98, 0.99, and 1.00. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with major ticks at 0.2 intervals. The Final Accuracy series is shown as a blue solid line with circular markers and vertical error bars; it starts near 0.93 at confidence 0.86, rises to around 0.98 at 0.89, stays in the high 0.96–1.00 range across most x-values, reaches about 1.00 around 0.98–0.99, and ends near 0.98 at 1.00. The Δ Accuracy series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers and vertical error bars; it begins around 0.28 at 0.86, declines to roughly 0.13–0.15 by about 0.90–0.91, shows a local increase near 0.20 at 0.92, drops to its lowest region around 0.05–0.07 near 0.94–0.95, then increases again to about 0.10–0.11 around 0.97–0.98, dips near 0.07 at 0.99, and ends around 0.20 at 1.00. The Initial Accuracy series is a green dash-dot line with square markers and vertical error bars; it starts near 0.64 at 0.86, increases through roughly 0.70–0.85 by about 0.88–0.91, dips to around 0.77 at 0.92, rises to about 0.90–0.92 around 0.94–0.96, stays near 0.88–0.92 through about 0.99, and then drops to roughly 0.77 at 1.00.
